title: 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT Electronic Engine Controls Map
introduction:
I use these views as the engine controls’ address book: first find the right neighborhood, then follow the callout to the exact component. The front view concentrates on the cam-timing controls and the air-duct sensor. The rear view spreads across the cylinder heads, intake hardware and exhaust sensors. The final transparent vehicle view locates the engine computer within the surrounding bodywork.

Start with the view heading, follow the leader line to the blue-highlighted part, and match the item label to that view’s table. Item labels restart between views, so keep each drawing paired with its own table. Keep LH/RH and intake/exhaust qualifiers attached to the component name; similar-looking hardware is easy to confuse when the viewpoint changes.

The useful distinction is between reporting conditions and carrying out commands. The powertrain control module uses sensor information to manage the engine, while actuators and solenoids perform controlled jobs. Variable camshaft timing changes valve timing; its oil-control solenoids belong to that control system. A location match identifies the component, not whether it works.

These drawings establish component identity and location relationships. Blue highlighting does not indicate a fault or a safe probe point, and transparent or omitted surrounding parts do not establish an access route. Use the matching service or diagnostic procedure before disconnecting, testing or replacing anything.

edits.why: Use the air duct and central throttle opening as visual landmarks, then follow each leader line to its highlighted component. Preserve the table’s bank and intake/exhaust distinctions when identifying the cam-timing controls.

The large flywheel and clutch assembly anchors this viewpoint. Follow the leader lines to the highlighted engine and exhaust components rather than judging by label placement alone. IMRC means intake manifold runner control; FRP means fuel rail pressure; CHT refers to cylinder-head temperature; KS means knock sensor. These terms clarify the labels without supplying a test method.

The transparent vehicle view places the highlighted PCM beside the strut-tower area of the engine bay. It supplies surrounding-location context rather than connector details or removal instructions. The PCM uses sensor information and stored control strategies to manage engine and powertrain functions.
